Subject: Request: client-facing data handling summary for Hosted API

Hi Irene,

Following up from our vendor review: Acme's security team has asked for a short, plain-language summary that we can share with internal stakeholders (procurement + legal) explaining how Redwood handles data for the Hosted API. Top items they want covered: subprocessors, cross-border transfers, retention/logs, and any customer controls exposed in the console (region selection, retention settings, subprocessor map link).

I've attached our redlined DPA for reference — it's heavy, so a 1-page summary plus a 1–2 line modal copy that can live in the console would be ideal. Can you confirm: (a) who on your side owns the copy and legal framing, and (b) if you can deliver a draft by EOD Tuesday (Aug 3)?

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_20270730.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Jillian Park

jillian.park@acme.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: plain-language summary + console modal copy (for Acme)

Irene — initial draft below. I kept the language as non-legal as possible and included short bullets. Please review and Laura/Marcus please flag any legal/product inaccuracies.

--- Plain-language summary (one page) ---
Redwood Hosted API — How we handle customer data (short version)

- What we process: We process text and binary inputs you send to the API to generate responses. We do not use customer data to train public models.
- Subprocessors: We work with a small set of subprocessors for cloud infrastructure, monitoring, and security. A current, downloadable subprocessor list is available in the console (link).
- Cross-border transfers: Customer data may be processed in multiple regions depending on your selected region and system routing. Transfers are governed by our DPA and standard contractual clauses where required; customers can select a preferred data residency region in the console for most workloads.
- Retention and logs: By default, short-lived logs (used for debugging and quality monitoring) are retained temporarily (e.g., up to 30 days) unless a customer opts into longer retention. Customers on dedicated/private deployments keep full control of retention settings.
- Controls in the console: Region selector, retention settings, subprocessor map, and the ability to request contract-level protections (e.g., SOC 2 reports).

--- Suggested console modal (2 lines) ---
Redwood processes requests in the region you select and works with a limited set of subprocessors. For details on data residency, subprocessors, and retention please see our Data Processing Addendum and the Subprocessors page (link).

Attachment: console_data_handling_draft.md (markdown)

Notes/questions for Laura: please confirm the retention period phrasing and whether we should reference SCCs explicitly or keep that to the DPA excerpts.

Thanks — Kim

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Draft: plain-language summary + console modal copy (for Acme)

Thanks, Kim — good clear draft. A few legal edits and suggestions below (inline):

- "We do not use customer data to train public models": Recommend we say "We do not use customer content to train models used outside of your deployment or for public model improvements, except where customers opt in" to cover opt-ins and dedicated/private exceptions.
- "Subprocessors": include a short sentence: "The Subprocessors page lists each vendor, function, and country of processing; customers can request additional details via the support portal."
- "Cross-border transfers": replace with: "Transfers are permitted as necessary for service delivery and are governed by our DPA. Where required, we rely on lawful transfer mechanisms such as adequacy findings and standard contractual clauses."
- "Retention and logs": avoid hard numbers unless product guarantees them. Suggest: "By default, transient logs are retained for a limited period for operational purposes; customers can request alternative retention policies under contract." If Product confirms 30 days, we can keep that as an example and mark as "typical".

I've attached a short extract from our DPA and a suggested modal wording with slightly more precise phrasing.

Attachment: DPA_excerpts_for_acme.docx (docx)

One more operational ask for Marcus: can you confirm whether the console currently displays a per-account Subprocessor map link and whether the region selector prevents routing outside the selected region for enterprise customers? If not, we should be transparent about routing fallbacks in the summary.

—Laura (legal)
